A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same delayed-sample temporal-difference method, convergence results and Baird experiments despite changed titles and terminology. The main texts, figures, equations and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 Section 7 reports original numerical experiments on Baird’s counterexample, including algorithm comparisons and gap-function sensitivity results in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: V2 Section 6 retains these original experiments in Figure 1. Appendix D supplies the environment description.

M1.justification: Direct GTD is renamed A_t^T TD, but the delayed two-sample update and its projected variant remain unchanged. The i.i.d. discussion is shortened and attributed to prior work without introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate off-policy prediction solely on the same seven-state Baird counterexample. Moving its description to Appendix D does not add coverage.

E2.justification: Both experimental comparisons use naive off-policy linear TD and GTD as baselines. The newly discussed historical A^T TD algorithm and related methods are not additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain 10,000 training steps, the NEU metric, constant learning rates selected from {0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05}, and the reported selection of 0.001. Environment parameters, initialization and plotted gap-function settings also match.

E4.justification: V1 Figure 3 and v2 Figure 1 right report the same sensitivity analysis of four gap functions, testing how slowly the sampling gap can grow without divergence. No additional ablation or robustness analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 30 independent runs with shaded standard errors. No new seed information, uncertainty procedure or statistical test is introduced.

E6.justification: V1 Figures 2–3 are retained as v2 Figure 1 with the same learning curves and findings: TD diverges, the proposed method initially drops faster and oscillates less than GTD, and some slower gap functions still permit convergence. No additional empirical results are reported.

T1.justification: The main guarantees and proofs are retained. V2 corrects Assumption 4.3 from C_alpha/(t+1)^(-nu) to C_alpha/(t+1)^nu and restores the squared norm in Lemma 9, formerly Lemma 11. It also qualifies the fixed-gap argument with a negative-definiteness caveat and replaces some background derivations. However, its new Section 3 estimator formula labels an estimate of -A^T as A^T.

C1.justification: V1 presents a new direct solution to double sampling and a novel refined ODE discretization as central contributions. V2 explicitly makes rediscovering and refining Sutton et al.’s A^T TD design the main contribution, while attributing the skeleton-iterates framework to Qian et al. (2024). It foregrounds the single parameter vector and learning rate, substantially redefining the novelty claim.

C2.justification: V2 strengthens the memory interpretation from reasonably small overhead to negligible cost in any empirical implementation, adding a hypothetical universe-age computation. It also distinguishes its memory from experience replay and discusses possible application of its analysis to kernel-loss methods. The explanations of the Baird results and qualifications about their limited generality remain.

D1.justification: The experimental settings and implementation disclosures are retained, with the Baird environment and initialization description moved to Appendix D. No code/data access information, actual execution hardware or runtime measurements are added.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises the relationship to prior research through its A^T TD lineage, new attribution to Qian et al. (2024), and citation of Yao (2023) for i.i.d. sampling. The detailed comparison with Guan et al.’s PER-ETD is removed, while experience replay, kernel-loss methods and additional off-policy literature receive new discussion.

P1.justification: The title, algorithm terminology, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Background explanations are condensed, the standalone i.i.d. section becomes a short discussion, and the asymptotic proof moves from the appendix into Section 4. References and technical appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: The document adopts substantially different typography, headers, author placement and denser page layout. V1’s two vertically stacked result figures become smaller side-by-side panels with a shared caption in v2 Figure 1; the Baird diagram moves to Appendix D as Figure 2. These are presentation changes to retained evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 improves attribution of the central ideas and corrects the learning-rate assumption and squared-norm lemma, while making the projected scope of the finite-sample analysis explicit in the abstract. These are useful gains without new empirical evidence or convergence guarantees. The improvement is limited by the new estimator sign inconsistency and the stronger blanket claim that memory overhead is negligible.
